name: Onion

schedule.notes: Slow growers; start very early. Or buy sets/transplants.
Can take a light frost. Trim tops to 4 in at transplant.
Nitrogen feeds bulb growth; stop feeding when tops start to fall.
When tops fall and brown, lift and cure in shade for 2 to 3 weeks.

harvest.cues: Tops have flopped over and started to brown. Lift on a dry day.
harvest.storageNotes: Cure 2 to 3 weeks dry and airy, then braid or net. Keeps 4 to 8 months at 35 to 45 F.

varieties.name: Patterson
varieties.notes: Long day. Excellent storage in northern climates.

varieties.name: Candy
varieties.notes: Intermediate day, works in most of the US. Sweet.

varieties.name: Texas Grano
varieties.notes: Short-day sweet for southern US (below latitude 35).

notes: Match daylength to your latitude: short-day (south of 35°N), intermediate (35–38°N), long-day (38°N+). Wrong daylength = no bulbs.
